title: Lane Kiffin Returns to LSU with Controversial Past in Focus
seoTitle: Lane Kiffin Returns to LSU Amid Past Controversy
subtitle: The former Alabama offensive coordinator faces the media as he takes over the LSU helm
excerpt: Lane Kiffin's return to LSU brings to light details of his turbulent stint at Alabama, including conflicts with Nick Saban.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Before taking charge at LSU, Lane Kiffin brought to light details of his turbulent stint at Alabama. John Talty's book, "Lane Being Lane: The Story of Lane Kiffin, College Football’s Agent of Chaos," describes how the former offensive coordinator became involved in conflicts with Nick Saban and behaviors that generated controversy.

What changed at Alabama in 2016

In 2016, Kiffin left Alabama during a moment of tension. The book reports that his departure was marked by issues that arose both on and off the field, leading to an end that was publicly described as a "mutual decision," but in reality reflected the need to "find a job elsewhere." The text highlights that Saban asked Kiffin to stay away from college students and sorority girls, amid rumors regarding the coach's personal life.

Behaviors that caught attention

The book describes episodes in which Kiffin frequented bars in Tuscaloosa, such as the Innisfree Irish Pub, where, on one occasion, an Alabama staff member had to retrieve a golf cart left behind by the coach. The narrative also mentions that Kiffin used a fake name, "Joey Freshwater," when recognized in public places.

Impact on the relationship with Nick Saban

Kiffin's attitudes caused discomfort for Saban, who noted that the coach called his staff's work "ass-chewings." Talty reports that, during a film session for the 2016 playoff semifinal game, Kiffin called plays the team had not yet practiced, which may have been the final breaking point.

Agent reaction and personal changes

Agent Jimmy Sexton, who also represents Saban, reportedly played a role in redirecting Kiffin's career, leading him to take the head coaching job at FAU instead of a position at Houston. The book points out that after years of alcohol consumption, Kiffin quit drinking, reconciled with his family, and adopted practices like hot yoga.

The return to LSU in 2025

With his debut scheduled for the game against Clemson, Kiffin's return to LSU brings to the surface a story that blends athletic success and personal challenges. Talty's book will be released four days before the coach's official debut in Baton Rouge, offering a detailed view of how the events of 2016 continue to influence his professional trajectory.

With information from NOLA.com, New York Post.
